items.body: Trial 7b overwrote trial 7a and the sheet kept no record. The version that smelled right is gone.
Linalool arrives from bergamot, from lemon, and from the pure isolate. A declaration needs the sum, and the sheet holds three unrelated cells.
The formula asks for 0.0003 g. The scale reads to 0.001 g. The sheet does not say to dilute, so the number gets rounded and the formula changes.

method.label: Method
method.title: Three moves, one engine
method.intro: Compose the juice, weigh it on the bench, then check compliance and cost before anything leaves the lab.

compose.title: Compose
compose.body: Write the formula. Dilutions below scale resolution convert themselves.

weigh.title: Weigh
weigh.body: The scale drives the session. Overshoot, and unpoured lines rescale.

verify.title: Verify and cost
verify.body: Allergens sum across sources. A bottle's cost is computed at the volume you plan.

compose.title: Adjust a line and watch the rest move
compose.body: The matrix holds the formula, its versions in full history, and the totals bar that never leaves the screen. When a target mass falls below what your scale can read, the engine converts the material to a standard dilution and takes the solvent out of the carrier, so nothing gets rounded into a different formula.
compose.interactiveHint: Move a slider. Every other line and every total is recomputed by the same engine the server uses.
compose.edgeAllMin: All three lines are at zero. The rest of the concentrate fills the batch.
compose.edgeRemainderZero: These three lines fill the concentrate. The remaining materials sit at zero.

weigh.title: The scale drives the session, not the other way round
weigh.body: Connect over Web Serial or Bluetooth and weigh line by line, with the reading large enough to trust across the bench. Overshoot a pour and the unpoured lines rescale proportionally on the spot, so one heavy drop costs you a recalculation instead of the batch.

comply.title: Compliance is a gate, not a footnote
comply.body: Allergens are summed across every source that carries them, then checked against the limit for your product category across all twelve. Peroxide risk on citrus and phototoxicity are flagged where the decision is made. Over the limit, the label is blocked rather than printed with a warning nobody reads.
comply.note: Standards data is imported by the lab operator; IFRA does not redistribute it and neither do we.

cost.title: What a bottle costs, at the volume you actually plan
cost.body: Costing runs at three levels: the concentrate, the diluted juice, and the packaged unit. Move the volume and the matrix returns COGS, wholesale, recommended retail and margin together, so a price is a decision with arithmetic behind it.

evaluate.title: Maceration takes weeks, so the lab keeps the clock
evaluate.body: Timers run at day 1, 7, 14 and 30, and the organoleptic sheet asks the same questions at T+0, T+30min, T+4h and T+24h: clarity, opalescence, solubility, what it became. Inventory tracks what is left, where it physically sits, and when it expires, and the encyclopedia turns a commercial fragrance you admire into an editable skeleton formula.

indie.title: You are launching a brand
indie.body: You need compliance evidence and a defensible cost per bottle before anything can legally and profitably ship. Both come out of the formula you are already writing, not a separate spreadsheet you maintain by hand.

items.a: The Free plan is free and stays free: three formulas, the material catalog, the matrix, inventory and the encyclopedia. Prices for Pro and Enterprise are not set yet, and billing is not switched on, so nothing asks for a card today.

items.q: Does it do the IFRA check for me?
items.a: It aggregates every allergen across every source in your formula, computes the percentage of the batch, and compares it against the limit for your product category, then blocks label generation when you are over. The standards data itself is imported by the operator of the lab, because IFRA does not permit redistributing it.
Anything reachable over Web Serial or Web Bluetooth on desktop and Android, and over Bluetooth LE on iOS through the mobile build. Drivers ship for SBI and Mettler, A&D, and a generic line protocol.

items.q: What happens when my scale cannot weigh the amount?
items.a: That is the case the engine was built for. Below your scale's resolution it converts the material to a standard dilution, computes the stock mass you can actually weigh, and subtracts that solvent from the carrier so the batch still lands on target.

items.q: Can other people see my formulas?
items.a: No. Isolation is enforced by PostgreSQL row-level security, and the API connects under a role that is not permitted to bypass it, so the guarantee does not depend on application code being correct. There is a test in the repository that proves one account cannot read another's rows.

items.q: Does it work on my phone, and offline?
items.a: It installs as a progressive web app and ships as an iOS and Android build through Capacitor. The interface and cached catalog work offline; weighing needs the scale, and syncing needs the network.

items.q: Can I get my data out?
items.a: Formulas, weighing records and compliance reports export to PDF and Excel, generated on the server. The project is open source under the MIT licence, so the schema is inspectable.

items.q: Is there any AI in here?
items.a: No, and deliberately not in the search: it runs on PostgreSQL full-text search with trigram matching and a descriptor-to-accord map built from co-occurrence, which is explainable and does not invent materials that do not exist.
